tasks.short: Read gas meters and keep receipt and dispensing records

steps.what: Read gas meters and capture identified readings
outputs: dated meter readings with units and flow direction

steps.what: Resolve meter resets, units and inconsistent gas quantities
inputs: dated meter readings with units and flow direction

steps.what: Maintain records using receipt and dispensing entry fields
Check recorded amounts against readings and save corrections
inputs: dated meter readings with units and flow direction

tasks.design: Configure an existing {OPS_SYSTEM} entry form with meter identifiers, units, reading dates and receipt/dispensing fields. The operator still reads meters and resolves unusual quantities; the form reduces repeated record entry without controlling gas equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings and movement records may require repeated headings and copying between current records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record templates and reusable meter fields can reduce repeated typing where the installed system supports them.
tasks.still_hard: Resets, pressure or temperature bases and questionable readings require operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a misleading reading before it becomes a trusted quantity.
tasks.altitude: From repeated entry toward checking the provenance of gas movement quantities.

reach.learn: Reuse meter identifiers while preserving manual reading checks.

evidence.claim: Native structured entry and reusable identifiers could reduce repeated gas record typing; this station-specific design and its time estimates are unmeasured.

assumptions: The boundary includes reading meters, resolving quantities, writing the required records and checking them.

The station operator produces meter identifier, timestamp, displayed value, unit and flow direction in s1; its full capture time is retained. Prior readings and configuration are existing station records maintained by station staff; missing metadata returns to manual investigation in s2.
Try the installed station system's native entry form first. No telemetry feed, automatic anomaly alert or control action is assumed.
The author's ordinary save and corrections remain within retained entry/checking time and need no separate approval.
unknowns: Whether today's station record already supplies these fields automatically.
How much record entry repeats information rather than capturing a new reading.
research_questions: Time several meter rounds and compare native entry with current records, including reset corrections and missing units.

already_counted.description: Check entered quantities and correct the saved record

incremental.description: Maintain meter field definitions and test template changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=85; gross saving 15 less 2 upkeep gives central net 13. Conservative case: meter/unit metadata need repeated manual completion, so s3 retains 27 of 30 hours; all other 70 remain, leaving 3 gross less 2 upkeep =1. Better supported case: compatible native fields retain 19 of 30 entry hours, giving 11 gross less 2 upkeep =9. Already automatic record entry has no eligible saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep meter interpretation and equipment accountability with the operator while reducing repeated record entry.
reach: Compare quantity-record templates with adjacent pumping roles.
role.ambitious_version: Reliable gas movement records with visible reading provenance.
